proposals.clause_text: Watch (b): Settlement with no admission of wrongdoing
proposals.summary: Ford agreed to pay $2.3 million under an EEOC conciliation agreement resolving a 2021 charge of race and national-origin harassment at its Buffalo stamping plant. The EEOC's investigation found reasonable cause to believe the harassment occurred.
proposals.caveat: The EEOC release does not mention an admission, and the conciliation agreement itself was not reviewed, so "no admission" is not confirmed. Same open question as Tesla: does an EEOC "reasonable cause" finding count as an "agency finding" under the Black rule? This screen treats it as NOT qualifying until the team decides.
proposals.tripwire: Team rules that EEOC cause findings qualify, or a court/agency adjudicates a violation -> propose Black under (b).

evidence.publisher: U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (press release)
evidence.quote: The EEOC's investigation found reasonable cause to believe that Ford personnel at the facility subjected numerous employees to harassment and discrimination based on race and national origin.

evidence.publisher: U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (press release)
evidence.quote: Following the EEOC's investigation, the parties engaged in the EEOC's pre-litigation conciliation process, resulting in a conciliation agreement.

proposals.clause_text: Watch (b): Settlement with no admission of wrongdoing
proposals.summary: Accenture agreed to pay $25 million to resolve DOJ False Claims Act allegations that its federal-services unit certified non-discrimination in federal contracts while taking race or sex into account in employment decisions. DOJ states the claims are allegations only.
proposals.tripwire: A court ruling, jury verdict, or agency finding that Accenture engaged in racial discrimination -> propose Black under (b).

evidence.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs (press release)
evidence.quote: to resolve alleged violations of the False Claims Act for failing to comply with anti-discrimination requirements in federal contracts and discriminating against employees and applicants for employment because of race or sex.

evidence.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs (press release)
evidence.quote: The claims resolved by the United States in the settlement are allegations only and there has been no determination of liability.

proposals.clause_text: Black (a) Knowingly spread false information to the public: Court ruling on the merits (including summary judgment on falsity), 2023-03-31 (within 7 years). Scope: court found the statements false; knowledge (actual malice) was not adjudicated
proposals.summary: Delaware Superior Court granted Dominion summary judgment on falsity: Fox News statements about Dominion and the 2020 election were false. Fox Corp and Fox News Network settled on April 18, 2023 (about $800M including a related suit, per Fox's filing).
proposals.caveat: The court decided falsity only. Actual malice (the "knowingly" part) was left for trial and never decided because the case settled. The ruling names Fox News Network, LLC, a Fox Corp subsidiary.

evidence.publisher: Superior Court of the State of Delaware (C.A. No. N21C-03-257 EMD)
evidence.quote: The evidence developed in this civil proceeding demonstrates that is CRYSTAL clear that none of the Statements relating to Dominion about the 2020 election are true. Therefore, the Court will grant summary judgment in favor of Dominion on the element of falsity.

evidence.publisher: Fox Corporation Form 10-Q (SEC EDGAR)
evidence.quote: On March 31, 2023, the court in the Dominion case issued its rulings on summary judgment motions that were unfavorable to the Company. Following these rulings, on April 18, 2023, the Company and its subsidiary, Fox News Network, LLC, entered into a Release and Settlement Agreement with Dominion

proposals.clause_text: Black (b) Engaged in discrimination on the basis of race, ethnicity, sexual orientation or gender identity: Jury verdict, even if later reduced, 2021-10-04 (within 7 years)
proposals.summary: A federal jury (N.D. Cal., Diaz v. Tesla) returned a verdict against Tesla on a former contingent worker's race-discrimination claims at the Fremont factory. Damages were later reduced ($136.9M to $15M to $3.175M after a retrial); the parties settled confidentially in March 2024.
proposals.caveat: NEW vs. the September starting list, which had TSLA on Watch. The rule counts "a jury verdict, even if later reduced", and October 2021 is inside the 7-year window (until 2028-10-04). The worker was a contingent (staffing-agency) worker. This is a proposal for the team to decide.

evidence.publisher: Tesla, Inc. Form 10-Q (SEC EDGAR)
evidence.quote: On October 4, 2021, in a case captioned Diaz v. Tesla, a jury in the Northern District of California returned a verdict against Tesla on claims by a former contingent worker that he was subjected to race discrimination

evidence.publisher: Tesla, Inc. Form 10-Q (SEC EDGAR)
evidence.quote: the damages awarded against Tesla were reduced from an initial $ 136.9 million (October 4, 2021) down to $ 15 million (April 13, 2022), and then further down to $ 3.175 million (April 3, 2023).

proposals.clause_text: Watch (b): Open lawsuit or agency complaint on (a) or (b) that has survived a motion to dismiss
proposals.summary: California Civil Rights Department suit (filed Feb 9, 2022) alleging systemic race discrimination at Fremont; first trial phase set for Sept 21, 2026. Separate EEOC suit (filed Sept 28, 2023) for race harassment and retaliation is in discovery. EEOC issued a cause finding on June 1, 2022.
proposals.caveat: Both suits are past the pleading stage (one set for trial, one in discovery). The 10-Q does not mention a motion to dismiss; "survived" is inferred from the trial setting and discovery. Whether the CRD trial actually began on Sept 21, 2026 was not confirmed from a primary source this run (calcivilrights.ca.gov refused scripted access). Open question for the team: does an EEOC "cause finding" count as an "agency finding" under the Black rule? This screen treats it as NOT qualifying until the team decides, because it is a preliminary determination, not an adjudication.
proposals.tripwire: A liability finding in the CRD trial or in EEOC v. Tesla (N.D. Cal.) -> propose Black under (b). If the Diaz proposal is approved, TSLA is already Black and this becomes context.

evidence.publisher: Tesla, Inc. Form 10-Q (SEC EDGAR)
evidence.quote: on February 9, 2022, the California Civil Rights Department ("CRD," formerly "DFEH") filed a civil complaint against Tesla in Alameda County, California Superior Court, alleging systemic race discrimination, hostile work environment and pay equity claims, among others.

evidence.publisher: Tesla, Inc. Form 10-Q (SEC EDGAR)
evidence.quote: The first phase of the trial is currently set for September 21, 2026. Additionally, on June 1, 2022, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission ("EEOC") issued a cause finding against Tesla that closely parallels the CRD's allegations.

proposals.clause_text: Watch (a): Open lawsuit or agency complaint on (a) or (b) that has survived a motion to dismiss
proposals.summary: Multistate attorneys-general case (N.D. Cal.) alleging Meta misled the public about risks of Instagram and Facebook to young users. Trial began Aug 18, 2026; a settlement of up to $17.1B was announced Aug 26, 2026, subject to court approval.
